title: Hawa 0.5 / Native workspace and live sync
style: Pinned Monad tokens; captions; no added title bars

chapters.title: Hawa 0.5
chapters.caption: Set up flow in Rhino. Connect Grasshopper controls. Inspect the same result.

chapters.title: A native Rhino workspace
chapters.caption: Open Hawa. Dock the panel. Setup, Solve and View keep the case controls together.

chapters.title: Select the bodies
chapters.caption: Use closed Rhino meshes or solid Breps. Fit the domain, then edit its origin and size.

chapters.title: Set the physical case
chapters.caption: Enter viscosity, density and speed. Choose each domain-face boundary. Native flow follows the global X axis.

chapters.title: Run, pause, cancel, reset
chapters.caption: Set cell size, target steps and backend. Run the embedded Python solver. This canopy capture shows 200 MPS steps.

chapters.title: Choose the field view
chapters.caption: Select speed or pressure. Set the slice axis and position. Use blue-green or spectrum colours and fixed limits.

chapters.title: Share the case with Grasshopper
chapters.caption: Hawa Linked Case connects the panel to GH. Direct sliders can update from either interface.

chapters.title: Keep one owner for each edit
chapters.caption: Computed GH inputs stay read-only in the panel. One Linked Case owns the binding. Physical edits invalidate old results.

chapters.title: Save the model and definition
chapters.caption: Save the .3dm and its bound .gh together. Reopening restores settings and stays idle. Missing bodies produce an error.

chapters.title: Resolve curved stationary walls
chapters.caption: Brep tessellation follows cell size and body scale. Enable interpolated stationary walls to use fractional wall-link distances.

chapters.title: Clip the visible boundary
chapters.caption: Supported slices now cut mixed cells at stored wall intersections. The old display discarded whole cells around the body.
chapters.note: Display correction / captured before and after

chapters.title: Read the wall colours correctly
chapters.caption: Boundary colours are reconstructed for display. Raw probe samples stay unchanged. Plane Field and Grid Preview keep their existing masks.

chapters.title: Three native starting points
chapters.caption: 21: linked block case. 22: selected canopy with GH controls. 23: curved sphere, operated from the Rhino panel.

chapters.title: Find tools by their operation
chapters.caption: The Hawa tab and icons group setup, solve and display tools. Hull construction stays in the example assembly.

chapters.title: Keep the wider GH toolbox
chapters.caption: Use domain wireframes, 3D flow tubes, contours, isosurfaces and surface fields. Share one Field Snapshot across time-matched views.

chapters.title: Load airfoils from local files
chapters.caption: Example 12 loads coordinates and polars. Generate four-digit NACA sections offline. Inspect the RC wing assembly.
chapters.note: Existing GH workflow / local data only

chapters.title: Search completed candidates
chapters.caption: Example 10 varies a parametric hull. Hawa Search advances after each completed result. Pause or cancel at solver checkpoints.
chapters.note: Existing asynchronous GH search / available in 0.5

chapters.title: Explore prescribed motion
chapters.caption: Examples 17–20 cover an oscillating cylinder, pitching foil, rotating paddle and cycle search. Body pose and fields share a capture time.

chapters.title: Compare a refinement patch
chapters.caption: Example 15 uses one fixed 2:1 patch. Check a uniform fine-grid reference before interpreting a result.
chapters.note: Existing experimental GH refinement / available in 0.5

chapters.title: Record the evolving flow
chapters.caption: Examples 13 and 16 save fields for playback. Keep colour limits fixed while you inspect the changing wake.

chapters.title: Open, change, repeat
chapters.caption: Start with the annotated definitions. Keep the domain, fluid and comparison time controlled when you change geometry.

chapters.title: Recover after a failed close
chapters.caption: Detached jobs stay in a shared cleanup queue. Failed close requests retry after GH closes. No native panel is required.

chapters.title: Check the work in Rhino
chapters.caption: 148 Python tests and 33 state contracts passed. Live failure tests covered all six cleanup paths. Final jobs, sessions and workers: zero.

chapters.title: Use the documented scope
chapters.caption: Native setup covers stationary, single-fluid flow. GH provides the broader workflows. These short examples demonstrate controls and output.
chapters.note: Experimental solver / compare grids, domains and physical time

chapters.title: Start with an example
chapters.caption: Open 21 for live sync, 22 for selected bodies, or 23 for curved walls. Read the build log and inspect the verification records.
